PASSO 1: comparação de diferença usa als: STEP 1: good news: German comparatives work almost like English ones: small → smaller = klein → kleiner; old → oldest = alt → am ältesten. STEP 2: the trap is "than" and "as": a difference uses «als» ("than"); equality uses «wie» ("as … as"). Never «größer wie». STEP 3: and German NEVER uses "more" with long adjectives: English "more beautiful", "more expensive", "more interesting" are simply «schöner», «teurer», «interessanter».
O português compara com palavras soltas:: English uses -er for short adjectives and "more" for long ones ("more expensive"). German always uses -er, no matter how long the adjective is: «interessanter», «komplizierter».
PASSO 1: para dizer «mais … do que», acr: STEP 1: to say "more … than", add «-er» to the adjective and use «als» for "than": «Berlin ist größer als München» (Berlin is bigger than Munich). STEP 2: many short adjectives take an UMLAUT: alt → älter; jung → jünger; groß → größer; stark → stärker; warm → wärmer; kalt → kälter. Compare English old → elder. STEP 3: adjectives in «-el», «-er» drop the «e»: teuer → teurer; dunkel → dunkler. STEP 4: IRREGULAR forms you need to memorize — mostly the same ones that are irregular in English: gut → besser (good → better); viel → mehr (much → more); gern → lieber (gladly → rather); hoch → höher; nah → näher. STEP 5: equality: «so … wie» (as … as): «Er ist so groß wie ich» (he's as tall as I am). STEP 6: with no second term: «Es wird kälter» (it's getting colder).

PASSO 1: para dizer «o mais …», há DUAS: STEP 1: to say "the most …", there are TWO forms. FORM 1: «am» + adjective + «-sten», after a verb like sein: «Der Zug ist am schnellsten» (the train is the fastest). FORM 2: «der/die/das» + adjective + «-ste» + noun, when the noun follows (with the adjective ending!): «der schnellste Zug» (the fastest train), «die schönste Stadt», «das beste Essen». STEP 2: adjectives ending in -d, -t, -s, -ß, -z, -sch take «-esten»: am ältesten, am heißesten. STEP 3: the umlaut comes along: am ältesten, am größten, am stärksten. STEP 4: irregular forms: gut → am besten (best); viel → am meisten (most); gern → am liebsten (most of all, favorite); hoch → am höchsten; nah → am nächsten. STEP 5: a typical sentence: «Im Sommer ist es am wärmsten» (it's warmest in summer). STEP 6: show the group with «von» or the genitive: «der schönste von allen» (the most beautiful of all).

PASSO 1: «mehr» e «weniger» comparam qua: STEP 1: «mehr» (more) and «weniger» (less, fewer) compare quantities: «Ich habe mehr Zeit als du» (I have more time than you), «Er hat weniger Geld» (he has less money). STEP 2: «immer» + comparative = more and more: «Es wird immer kälter» (it's getting colder and colder). STEP 3: «gern, lieber, am liebsten» are the same kind of family as «gut, besser, am besten»: I like, I prefer, I like most. «Ich trinke lieber Tee» = I'd rather drink tea. STEP 4: the comparative also goes before a noun and takes an ending: «ein größeres Haus» (a bigger house), «die besseren Schuhe». STEP 5: equality and difference: «so … wie» (as … as) and «anders als» (different from).

O comparativo de klein se forma com -er:: The comparative of «klein» is formed with -er: kleiner. You don't drop the e of the ending with this adjective.
No comparativo de groß, a vogal o recebe: In the comparative of «groß», the o takes an umlaut and you add -er: größer.
O superlativo adverbial de alt é am älte: The adverbial superlative of «alt» is «am ältesten»: umlaut on the a and an extra e before -sten, giving ältesten.
Gut tem comparativo irregular: besser. N: «Gut» has an irregular comparative: besser — just like good → better. It is never «guter».
Depois do comparativo größer, usa-se als: After the comparative «größer», use «als» (than) to compare a difference: Tom ist größer als Lena.
A construção de igualdade é so ... wie:: The construction for equality is «so … wie» (as … as): Lena ist so alt wie Tom.
